info.title: AI Accessibility Automation Agent — Dashboard API
info.description:
Backend API of the **AI Accessibility Automation Agent** dashboard: scans, live job status, saved reports, manual audit reviews, VPAT/ACR exports, compliance checklists, the remediation backlog and scripted journeys. Every operation in this document was taken from the Express routers in `src/api/routes/*.js` (mounted in `src/api/app.js:33-46`) and cross-checked against the code; `x-source` on each operation gives the file and line numbers.

## URLs
- **Swagger UI:** `http://localhost:<PORT>/api-docs` (loads Swagger UI from cdn.jsdelivr.net, so internet access is needed).
- **Raw OpenAPI JSON:** `http://localhost:<PORT>/api/openapi.json` (file: `docs/openapi.json`).
- Start the server with `npm start` (`node src/server.js`). It listens on **127.0.0.1 only** (src/server.js:17) on `PORT`, default **4173** (src/config.js:60). The server URL below is `/`, so requests go to the server that served this document.
- The dashboard UI itself is served at `/` from `public/` (src/api/app.js:36); it is not part of this API.

## Authentication and access control
There is **no authentication or authorization**: no login, API key, session or security scheme (src/api/middleware/local-request-guard.js:4). The `auth` object of `POST /api/scans` holds credentials for the *website under test*, not for this API. The only access control is the local request guard, which runs first for every request including static files (src/api/app.js:33; see `x-local-request-guard`):
- **Host allow-list:** the `Host` header's hostname (port ignored) must be `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]` or a comma-separated `DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_HOSTS` entry, otherwise **421** `{"error":"This dashboard only accepts requests addressed to localhost."}`. This defends against DNS rebinding.
- **Origin check:** for methods other than GET, HEAD and OPTIONS, an `Origin` header, when present, must have an allowed hostname, otherwise **403** `{"error":"Cross-origin requests are not allowed."}`. Requests without `Origin` (curl, server-side clients) are not checked.
- No CORS headers are sent, so a page on another origin cannot read responses. Browsers do not let scripts set `Host` or `Origin`, so they are described here rather than offered as parameters.

## Request bodies
JSON bodies are parsed by `express.json({ limit: "1mb" })` (src/api/app.js:34): only `Content-Type: application/json` is parsed; with another type the body is ignored and each route reports its "missing body" error. Malformed JSON or a top-level primitive gives 400 `The request contains invalid JSON.`; a body over 1 MB gives 413; a non-UTF charset or unknown `Content-Encoding` gives 415.

## Errors
JSON errors are always `{"error": string}` with status `error.status`, else 404 for filesystem ENOENT, else 500 (src/api/middleware/error-handler.js:3-8). URLs in messages are sanitised; filesystem paths in ENOENT messages are **not**, so 404 messages can contain absolute server paths. Unmatched paths and wrong methods (for example `GET /api/scans`) get Express's default **HTML** 404 `Cannot <METHOD> <path>`; there is no 405. The exception is `OPTIONS` on a routed path: Express answers it with 200 `text/plain`, listing the allowed methods in the body and in an `Allow` header (for example `POST` for `/api/scans`; verified at runtime). Every GET route also answers HEAD, and JSON responses carry a weak `ETag` (Express defaults), so conditional requests may return 304.

## Jobs
Scan and journey jobs live in memory in one map per server process (src/api/app.js:25,32): they are lost on restart, and finished jobs older than 24 hours are removed whenever a new scan is posted (src/api/routes/scans.js:11,75-77). Saved reports in `reports/` persist.

## Conventions in this document
- `x-source`: source file and line numbers the operation was verified against.
- `x-unconfirmed`: a schema or behaviour that could not be fully established from the implementation; the description says which parts are confirmed.
- `x-express-route`: the Express route when it differs from the documented path. The generic `GET /api/reports/:id/:section` route is documented as 12 concrete paths (one per allowed section) so each response has its own schema; the `/reports/...` static mount is marked `STATIC`.
- Examples are synthetic (`*.example.test` hosts, placeholder ids); several large examples are abbreviated, as noted in their descriptions.

servers.description: The server that serves this document (default http://localhost:4173).

allowedHosts: each comma-separated entry of DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_HOSTS (trimmed, lower-cased)
x-local-request-guard.hostCheck: Every request: the Host header's hostname (port ignored; bracketed IPv6 kept) must be on the allow-list, otherwise 421 {"error":"This dashboard only accepts requests addressed to localhost."}.
x-local-request-guard.originCheck: Methods other than GET, HEAD and OPTIONS that send an Origin header: the Origin hostname must be on the allow-list (an unparsable Origin, including "null", fails), otherwise 403 {"error":"Cross-origin requests are not allowed."}. Requests without Origin pass.

The dashboard calls it before it sends any scan or login data (public/features/scan.js:66-76). post.description:
Validates the request, creates an in-memory job and answers **202** with the job snapshot, then runs the scan in the background: Playwright crawl, axe-core and other checks, optional AI and optional live NVDA (src/api/routes/scans.js:19-101). Poll `GET /api/jobs/{id}` for progress; once `reportId` is set, load the report endpoints.

After the 202, failures (login failure, browser launch, TLS...) are reported only through the job (`status: failed`, `error`). No `Location` header is set and there is no idempotency key, so re-sending after a lost response starts a duplicate scan. Several scans can run at once.

**Side effects:** removes finished jobs (scan or journey) whose `updatedAt` is more than 24 hours old (scans.js:75-77); clears `auth.password` in the parsed body (scans.js:73); creates `reports/<reportId>/` with evidence screenshots and checkpoint files `vpat_draft.json` and `summary.json`, plus `ACR_VPAT_Report.csv` / `.html` on completion (src/scanner/crawl/run.js:30-32; src/report/export.js:8-32); opens a real browser (headed when NVDA is requested), may log in to the target site and load or save an encrypted session; sends page data to OpenAI when AI is effective; on a **complete** scan only, updates the site's remediation backlog (scans.js:91-93; src/report/backlog.js:80-123). The written files become reachable under `/reports/`.

Defaults differ from the CLI: `maxPages` 10 (CLI: `MAX_PAGES` or 25) and `maxDepth` 2 (CLI: `MAX_DEPTH` or 3).

post.description:
Appends one documented review decision to `reports/<id>/audit-reviews.json` and returns the whole report re-read after the write, **without** the `interrupted` status rewrite (src/api/routes/reports.js:25-28; src/report/store.js:67-92). The decision can target a WCAG criterion, a manual check, a financial scenario step, a Section 508 / EN 301 549 VPAT row or a compliance-checklist item.

The report id is validated before the body, so an invalid id gives 400 `Invalid report id.` even when the body is also invalid. Without `Content-Type: application/json` the body is ignored and the request fails with 400 `A review object is required.`

**Side effects:** the full previous history plus the new record is written to a temporary file and renamed over `audit-reviews.json`; appends to one report are serialised (store.js:69-91). Nothing is ever edited or removed; the latest documented decision per target wins. `vpat_draft.json` is not modified.

get.summary: Download the report as JSON, ACR CSV or ACR HTML
get.description:
Renders the report on demand as an attachment named `accessibility-draft-<id>.<format>` (src/api/routes/reports.js:30-39). Allowed for reports in any status. The report is loaded before the format is checked, so a missing report gives 404 ENOENT even for an unknown format. Nothing is written to disk. The files written at scan completion (`ACR_VPAT_Report.csv` / `.html`) are separate and reachable through the static route.

- `json`: the full report (`readReport` result) pretty-printed with 2-space indent; the stored status is **not** rewritten to `interrupted`.

Files written by the application include `<reportId>/vpat_draft.json` (full report), `<reportId>/summary.json` (`{ id, targetUrl, startedAt, completedAt, status, summary }`), `<reportId>/ACR_VPAT_Report.csv` and `.html` (completed and NVDA-stopped scans), `<reportId>/evidence/...` screenshots, `<reportId>/audit-reviews.json`, `<reportId>/vpat-profile.json` (src/report/export.js:8-32; src/report/store.js:80-86,140-144; src/scanner/crawl/run.js:30-32), `_backlog/<host>.json` (src/report/backlog.js:32-35) and `_compliance/<id>.json` (src/report/compliance.js:63-65).

`serve-static` defaults apply (verified at runtime): GET and HEAD only; dotfiles ignored; a folder without a trailing slash redirects (301); a missing file falls through to Express's HTML 404 `Cannot GET <path>`. ETag, `If-None-Match` and `Range` are supported. The `evidenceUrl` / `evidence.url` values returned by the API point here.

ActionExclusions.description:
"Do not click" entries (labels, or URL / host / path-suffix rules) that the crawler must never activate inside the target application's origin. Validated by `parseActionExclusions` (src/browser/action-exclusions.js:33-41):

- A **string** is split on line breaks and on commas, except commas inside double quotes (`"No, thanks"`), after a backslash (`No\, thanks`) or inside the query of a URL entry (action-exclusions.js:3-31). An **array** is not split.
- Entries are whitespace-collapsed and trimmed; blanks and duplicates are removed.
- More than 100 distinct entries: 400 `Use at most 100 Do not click entries; no entries were applied.` Any entry over 2048 characters: 400 `Each Do not click entry must be at most 2048 characters; entries are never truncated.`
- Any other type: 400 `Do not click entries must be text or a list of strings.`; a non-string array item: 400 `Every Do not click entry must be text.`
- `null` or an omitted field means no entries.
- The entries are then merged with the server's `EXCLUDE_ACTION_LABELS` (server entries first) and re-validated, so the 100-entry limit counts both; merge errors get the suffix ` Entries from EXCLUDE_ACTION_LABELS also count.` (src/api/routes/scans.js:31-33; src/api/routes/journeys.js:29-30; action-exclusions.js:45-47).

oneOf.description: One entry per line; commas also separate entries (see above).
One entry per item; items are not split.

When `enabled` is truthy, `loginUrl`, `username` and `password` are required (scans.js:36-45).

Oversized strings are **silently truncated**, never rejected (scans.js:47-55). After the scan configuration is built, `auth.password` in the parsed request body is overwritten with an empty string (scans.js:73); credentials never appear in the job.

password.description: Required when enabled; must not be empty (not trimmed), same 400 message (scans.js:43). Truncated to 2048 characters (scans.js:49). Never returned.

persist.description: Only an explicit `false` disables saving and reusing the encrypted session (scans.js:50).

The history in `audit-reviews.json` is append-only; the latest documented decision per target wins (audit.js:68; src/scanner/wcag.js:99; src/report/vpat.js:114; src/report/financial.js:99). Raw history (`auditReviews`, the `reviews` section) can contain entries that later fail documentation checks.

Score.description: Heuristic observed-health score (`assessReport`, src/report/assessment.js:32-82). Not a WCAG conformance score.

score.description: 0-10 with one decimal; `null` when the report has no `completedAt`, no successfully scanned page or no observed state (assessment.js:55-56).

ReportOverview.description: Overview section (src/report/assessment.js:86-89). Keys whose stored value is missing are omitted.

PagesSection.x-unconfirmed: Page record shape comes from the crawler and was not fully traced.
PagesSection.description: Pages section: `{ pages: report.pages || [] }` (src/report/assessment.js:92). **Partially confirmed:** page records are open objects.

ActivitySection.description: Activity section: the report's stored events (src/report/assessment.js:94).

AcrSection.description: ACR section: `{ rows: report.acr }`, where `acr` is `audit.criteria` (src/report/assessment.js:95; src/report/store.js:56).

EvidenceFinding.description: Finding reference in the evidence section (src/report/assessment.js:117-123).

target.description: Copied from the finding: string or array.

EvidenceSection.description: Findings grouped by screenshot across issues, needs-review items and best practices (src/report/assessment.js:112-152).

evidence.description: Relative file inside the report folder.

evidenceUrl.description: `/reports/<id>/evidence/[baselines/]<file>.(png|jpg|jpeg|webp)`, or null when the path fails validation (assessment.js:148-151). Served by the static route `GET /reports/{reportId}/{filePath}`.

AssistiveTechnologySection.x-unconfirmed: metadata.actualRuns entries and screen-reader state records come from the assistive-technology modules and were not traced.
AssistiveTechnologySection.description: Assistive-technology section (src/report/assessment.js:97-107). **Partially confirmed:** `summary` is confirmed; `metadata`, `runs` and `states` items are open objects.

ComparisonFinding.description: One finding occurrence per WCAG criterion (src/report/comparison.js:84-113). `surface` and `reviewKey` are internal composite keys separated by U+0000 characters (JSON `\u0000`).

target.description: Selector parts joined with ` → `, or `Unknown element`.

page.description: Route key: path + search + hash route.

ComparisonGraph.description: Normalised crawl graph; only edges whose ends are both nodes are kept (src/report/comparison.js:71-82).

ComparisonResult.description: Result of `compareReports` (src/report/comparison.js:7-69). Each group is sorted by criterion (numeric), then page, then target.

domain.description: Lower-case hostname shared by both reports.

excludedForCoverage.description: Findings skipped because the other scan did not cover that page and state.

excludedForReview.description: Findings skipped because the other scan has a pending needs-review item for the same surface, criterion and rule.

VpatProfileInput.description: Product details for the VPAT 2.5 exports. All fields are optional; unknown fields are dropped and missing ones are saved as `""`. Each value is converted with `String(value ?? "")`, control characters U+0000-U+0008, U+000B, U+000C and U+000E-U+001F are removed, and the value is trimmed; the length limit applies to that cleaned value, otherwise 400 `<field> must be at most <limit> characters.` (src/report/store.js:122,133-138).

reportDate.description: Empty or `YYYY-MM-DD`, otherwise 400 `Report date must be YYYY-MM-DD.`; only the format is checked (store.js:139).

VpatProfileStored.description: Contents of `reports/<id>/vpat-profile.json` returned as-is without re-validation, or `{}` when none has been saved (src/report/store.js:124-128).

ComplianceSource.x-unconfirmed: Keys come from the shipped data file src/report/compliance-data/public-sources.json; the code passes them through without validation.
ComplianceSource.description: Public source cited by the built-in checklists (passed through by src/report/compliance.js:30).

ComplianceSetSummary.description: Checklist with its `items` array replaced by the item count (src/api/routes/compliance.js:12). Built-in: `gigw-3.0` (78 items) and `sebi-digital-accessibility` (42 items). Imported sets also have `importedAt` (src/report/compliance.js:28,64).

retrievedOn.description: Date the public sources were retrieved.

ComplianceImportItem.description: Checklist item to import. Text values are cleaned: control characters become spaces, whitespace is collapsed, the value is trimmed and then **silently truncated** to the stated length (src/report/compliance.js:125-127).

reference.description: Required, truncated to 120 characters. An item without reference or requirement gives 400 `Item N needs a reference and a requirement.` (compliance.js:54-56).

wcag.description: Array, or a string split on `;`, `,` or whitespace. Only values matching `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$` are kept; others are dropped silently (compliance.js:60).

source.description: Truncated to 200 characters; defaults to the set title.

ComplianceImportRequest.description: Custom checklist (for example a licensed IS 17802 checklist), validated by `importComplianceSet` (src/report/compliance.js:42-67). A missing body (for example one sent without `Content-Type: application/json`) gives 400 `A checklist is required.` (compliance.js:43). A JSON array passes that check and fails on its missing `id` instead: 400 `Checklist id must be 2–60 lowercase letters, digits, dots or dashes.` (verified at runtime). Items come from `items` (JSON) or, when `format` is `csv`, from the CSV text in `csv`; 1 to 1000 items are allowed (400 `The checklist has no items.` / `A checklist may contain at most 1000 items.`). Item ids are generated from the reference and row number; `confidence` is always `imported`.

id.description: Trimmed and lower-cased, then must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{1,60}$` (2 to 61 characters, although the error message says 2-60), otherwise 400 `Checklist id must be 2–60 lowercase letters, digits, dots or dashes.` A built-in id gives 400 `That id belongs to a built-in checklist.` An imported set with the same id is **replaced without warning** (compliance.js:44-46,65).

title.description: Required. Trimmed and truncated to 200 characters; blank gives 400 `A checklist title is required.` (compliance.js:47-48).

publisher.description: Cleaned and truncated to 200 characters; default `""` (compliance.js:64).

format.description: Exactly `csv` switches to CSV mode; any other value or none uses `items` (compliance.js:49).

csv.description: CSV mode only. RFC 4180 quoting (`""` for a quote), CR / LF / CRLF line endings, blank rows skipped. The first non-blank row is a header matched by trimmed lower-case name and must include `reference` and `requirement`, otherwise 400 `CSV needs a header row with at least reference and requirement columns.`; optional columns `title`, `category`, `wcag`, `verification`, `source` (compliance.js:96-123). A missing `csv` yields no items.

items.description: JSON mode. A `null` entry causes a 500 (verified at runtime: `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'reference')`, src/report/compliance.js:54). Other non-object entries, such as a string, have no `reference` and give 400 `Item N needs a reference and a requirement.` (verified at runtime; compliance.js:54-56).

RelatedWcag.description: Scan status of a WCAG criterion linked to a checklist item, for reference only (src/report/compliance.js:81).

status.description: The report's criterion status (`Supports`, `Partially Supports`, `Does Not Support`, `Not Applicable`, `Not Evaluated`) or `Not in scope`.

findings.description: Confirmed findings mapped to the criterion.

ComplianceItem.x-unconfirmed: Built-in item keys appliesTo, sourceTitle, sourceUrl and the confidence values high/medium come from the shipped data file, not from code.
ComplianceItem.description: Checklist item with this report's decision (src/report/compliance.js:77-82). Decisions are never automatic; they come from `compliance-item` reviews posted to `POST /api/reports/{id}/reviews`.

review.description: Latest `compliance-item` review for this target with an allowed status and non-blank reviewer, notes and scope; otherwise null (compliance.js:79-80).

ComplianceSet.description: Checklist with full items and decision counts (src/report/compliance.js:76-85).

BacklogHistoryEntry.description: `added`: `{ at, change, reportId, note }` (src/report/backlog.js:97,135). `status`: `{ at, change, from, to, reportId?, note? }` (backlog.js:105,151). `owner` / `notes` / `dueDate`: `{ at, change, from, to }` (backlog.js:158). At most 100 entries are kept after a PATCH (backlog.js:161).

BacklogItem.description: Remediation item (src/report/backlog.js:67-75,97,135). Stored items are returned as they are in the file (backlog.js:40).

key.description: First 16 hex characters of the SHA-1 of rule id, target and page scope (backlog.js:18-22).

category.description: The finding's category, else `needs-review` for needs-review findings, else `wcag`.

latestScanReportId.description: Set by a sync when the item was not found in that report (backlog.js:117).

notFoundAwaitingVerification.description: `latestScan` is `not-found` and status is not `verified`, `wont-fix` or `false-positive`.

syncedReports.description: Report ids already applied; the file keeps the last 50 (backlog.js:56).

reportId.description: Coerced with `String(body.reportId || "")`; missing or invalid gives 400 `Invalid report id.` (src/api/routes/backlog.js:24; src/report/store.js:95).

BacklogSyncResult.description: src/report/backlog.js:86,121. When the report was already applied every count is 0 and `alreadySynced` is true.

findingId.description: Id of an entry in the report's `issues`, `incomplete` or `bestPractices`, otherwise 400 `That finding does not belong to this report.` (src/report/backlog.js:127-128).

BacklogItemUpdate.description: Fields to change; all optional and unknown fields ignored. A missing, non-object or array body gives 400 `An update object is required.` (src/report/backlog.js:143). Text values are converted with `String(value ?? "")`, control characters other than tab / LF / CR are removed, the value is trimmed and **silently truncated** to the limit; `null` clears a field to `""` (backlog.js:189-191). Each change is recorded in `history`. An empty `{}` still rewrites the backlog file.

status.description: Otherwise 400 `Status must be one of: open, in-progress, fixed, verified, reopened, wont-fix, false-positive.` Any status may change to any other, except that `verified` is refused while `latestScan` is `present`: 400 `The latest scan still found this defect. Fix it and run a new scan before marking it verified.` (backlog.js:148-152).

note.description: Up to 1000 characters; recorded only in the status-change history entry (backlog.js:151).

dueDate.description: Truncated to 10 characters first, then must be `""` or match `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$`, otherwise 400 `Due date must be YYYY-MM-DD.`; so `2026-12-31T10:00:00Z` is stored as `2026-12-31`. The date itself is not checked (backlog.js:154-157).

startUrl.description: Sanitised: credentials and sensitive query parameters removed (src/url-security.js:9-31).

JourneyInvalid.description: Journey file that failed to load or validate (src/journeys/runner.js:221; validation in src/journeys/journey.js:19-62). A missing test-data file gives a raw ENOENT message that can include an absolute path.

JourneyListEntry.description: One `*.json` file directly inside the project's `journeys/` folder.

file.description: File name in `journeys/` (no folders). Coerced with `String(body.file || "")`; a non-matching name gives 400 `Choose a journey file from the journeys folder.`; a file not listed gives 404 `Journey file not found.`; an invalid journey gives 400 with its validation error (src/api/routes/journeys.js:19-25).

ReportId.name: id
ReportId.description: Report id: the report folder name under `reports/`. Must match `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`, otherwise 400 `Invalid report id.` (src/report/store.js:95).

PreviousReportId.name: previousId
PreviousReportId.description: Id of the older baseline report (same rules as `id`).

JobId.name: id
JobId.description: Job id from the 202 response of `POST /api/scans` or `POST /api/journeys/run`. Not a report id. Looked up exactly in the in-memory job map (src/api/routes/scans.js:14).

BacklogHost.name: host
BacklogHost.description: Site hostname, e.g. `app.example.test`. Lower-cased by the route, then must match `^[a-z0-9.-]+$`, otherwise 400 `Invalid site name.` (src/api/routes/backlog.js:10,17,40; src/report/backlog.js:33). IPv6 hosts cannot have a backlog.

BacklogItemKey.name: key
BacklogItemKey.description: Backlog item key (16 lower-case hex characters for items created by this application). Matched exactly; not format-validated (src/report/backlog.js:145).

HostNotAllowed.description: Misdirected Request. The `Host` header's hostname is not `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]` or a `DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_HOSTS` entry (src/api/middleware/local-request-guard.js:3,9-11). Applies to every request, including static files.

example.error: This dashboard only accepts requests addressed to localhost.

CrossOriginRejected.description: The request (any method other than GET, HEAD or OPTIONS) has an `Origin` header whose hostname is not allowed, or that cannot be parsed (including `null`) (src/api/middleware/local-request-guard.js:12-16). Requests without `Origin` are not checked.

example.error: Cross-origin requests are not allowed.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The JSON body is larger than 1 MB (`express.json({ limit: "1mb" })`, src/api/app.js:34). Message from the body-parser dependency (verified at runtime).

example.error: request entity too large

UnsupportedBodyEncoding.description: The JSON body uses a non-UTF charset or an unsupported `Content-Encoding`. Messages from the body-parser dependency (verified at runtime).

ServerError.description: Unexpected error. The handler maps errors without `status` and without code `ENOENT` to 500 and returns the sanitised message (src/api/middleware/error-handler.js:3-8). Known triggers, where any, are listed in each operation's description.

example.error: Unexpected server error.
